The current legacy analog infrastructure limits scalability, resilience, and interoperability. Under this Call for Solutions, the selected vendor will deliver, integrate, install, and acceptance-test a flexible, open-standard, modular Digital IF solution across up to twenty (20) worldwide satellite communications (SATCOM) teleport sites. Increment 1 will establish a fully operational baseline designed to support subsequent capability upgrades and integrations in future fiscal years. SECTION 2 – REQUIREMENT DESCRIPTION PROBLEM STATEMENT Area of Interest: Modular Digital Intermediate Frequency Solu

quires an open-standard Digital IF architecture. However, before committing to a full-scale global deployment, the DoW must validate the operation, interoperability, security, and performance of these modular commercial solutions in a rigorous representative environment. Technical Objective & Scope The DoW seeks a commercial solution for an Increment 1 Digital IF capability set built on a flexible, open standard (e.g., Digital Intermediate Frequency Interoperability compliant), modular architecture. The selected solution will undergo standard site acceptance testing and operational verification to confirm compliance with contract performance requirements and site compatibility. Upon successful acceptance, this operational configuration will serve as the standardized baseline for deployment and installation across up to twenty (20) worldwide SATCOM teleport sites. Mission Impact Successful validation and deployment of this flexible open-standard Digital IF architecture will directly enhance warfighter lethality and survivability by delivering a highly resilient, agile, and survivable GEO-SATCOM capability which rapidly adapts to contested/congested environments. earch- grade data quality. • Formulate strategic pavement research plans advancing the LTPP program, conduct targeted performance case studies, and deliver practical engineering tools, Section 508- compliant publications, and technical webinars. • Develop and curate specialized, analysis-ready datasets for machine learning (ML) and predictive modeling across LTPP and broader highway infrastructure domains, integrating modern database architectures and coordinating data schemas with web portal contractors for public release. To meet these ESR bunch injection schemes and requirements, an array of stripline-based kickers, individually fed by high voltage (HV) pulse signals of up to +/-30 kV, will be installed in the ESR. The required deflection angle is in the range 1- 1.5 mrad, for the individual stripline kicker we target a deflection angle of ~125 µrad @ 18 GeV, assuming +/-27 kV pulse supply voltage between the kicker electrodes. To keep the losses of the stored beam low, a ~15 σ distance between the stored beam and the injection septa in the ESR must be maintained, which translates into a minimum physical aperture of 30 mm diameter for the stripline kickers. Reclamation-wide deployment software/platform/tools will be pursued during subsequent years at Reclamation’s discretion to realize the long-term benefits. The purpose of this system is to detect anomalies in real-time through comparison of historical process conditions and real-time information; and also provide the means for users to access this data; to display high-quality graphics; plot and trend this data; and provide notification of equipment performance anomalies. The anomaly detection system must be designed to accommodate very large real-time and historical databases so that multiple anomaly detection models can be run simultaneously. The models must be scalable and efficient so that they can run at any interval up to once every 1 minute, as required by the end user. The results of all calculations must be stored on-line for years, in its original resolution preferably within Reclamation’s historian. The archive results must not in any way affect the calculated data from its original resolution and sampled state. With this high-resolution data available, users can view both the plant conditions and analytic results while providing a very clear and accurate picture of past operations. The system must also provide a method for managing and dispositioning alarms. Any dispositioned alarm should be easily accessible; users should be able to bring up a full analytic copy of all alarm information associated with a dispositioned alarm.
